summary: Unexpected routing to edge-cpu-fallback causing long-tail latency and memory thrashing for NovaDocs prod
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (NovaDocs, enterprise/dedicated) reports a sudden tail-latency regression and increased 504s starting 2026-03-12 11:20 UTC. Traffic that should be routed to their pinned dedicated GPU variant is intermittently routed to an edge-cpu-fallback replica in us-west-2. The edge-cpu variant exhibits long cold-start times (~6–12s P99) and memory thrashing (OOM+swap churn) when model shards load, causing end-to-end request timeouts for NovaDocs API calls.

Impact:
- Customer-facing API calls experience P99 jump from ~350ms to 8–12s and increased 504 rate from 0.01% to 1.8% for a subset of requests.
- Affects critical document-embedding and summarization endpoints used in production.
- High-severity for customer (enterprise contractual SLA).

Environment:
- NovaDocs dedicated pool in prod (us-west-2) with regional failover enabled.
- Routing policy: primary -> dedicated-gpu-1; fallback policies include edge-cpu-fallback and remote-mirror.
- Observed during a traffic surge (daily peak) and a recent config change to autoscaler weights.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Send 200 concurrent summarization requests (avg prompt len 250 tokens) to NovaDocs route via prod API key.
2) Observe routing decisions in routing logs and downstream replica logs.
3) Correlate high-latency traces with edge-cpu-fallback pod start timestamps.

Observed behavior:
- Requests routed to edge-cpu-fallback replicas show large JVM/OS-level page faults and repeated mmap/disk reads during model load.
- KV-cache cold misses spike for routed requests (cache-hit drops from 98% to 44%).
- Autoscaler appears to have reduced dedicated-gpu weight after a short spike, enabling fallback activation.

Expected behavior:
- Routing should prefer warmed dedicated GPU replicas; fallback should only be used when dedicated capacity is exhausted and edge-cpu should serve only low-QPS, short requests without causing mass cold-starts.

Initial hypothesis:
- Recent autoscaler policy tweak (weight decay on busy nodes) caused premature diversion to fallback.
- Edge-cpu variant uses an older quantized artifact with different kernel selection, exacerbating cold-load memory usage and causing swap thrash.
- Combined effect of prefix cache eviction and fallback ramp creates serial cold-starts and long-tail latency.

Attachments / Links:
- Grafana latency dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/latency/prod-novadocs
- Routing log sample: s3://redwood-logs/nova/routing/2026-03-12-11-22.json
- Snapshot of pod logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/nova/edge-cpu-fallback/pod-logs-2026-03-12T11-22.gz

2026-03-12 12:05 UTC — Marco Hernandez (SRE): Confirmed tail-latency increase on NovaDocs route. Routing events show ~12% of traffic diverted to edge-cpu-fallback between 11:20–11:50 UTC. Kicked off pod-level telemetry capture.

2026-03-12 12:40 UTC — SRE Team (thread #support): Observed autoscaler weight decay event at 11:18 UTC (commit 9f2c3e4). Suspect that fast weight decay + short cooldown caused fallback activation. Collecting kernel vmstat and dmesg from edge-cpu pods.
2026-03-12 13:10 UTC — Aisha Patel (Support): Customer accepted temporary workaround to pin routing to dedicated-gpu-1 for critical routes while we investigate. Asking for ETA on permanent fix.

2026-03-12 14:30 UTC — Marco Hernandez (SRE): Implemented emergency routing override for NovaDocs (pin to dedicated-gpu-1). Observed metrics return to baseline within 3 minutes. Continuing root-cause analysis.

2026-03-13 09:20 UTC — Runtime Engineer, Priya Singh: Reproduced local load with quantized artifact and confirmed higher peak RSS on edge-cpu artifact due to older allocator behavior. Preparing patch to harmonize kernel selection and reduce mapped file churn.
investigation_notes: Telemetry: Edge-cpu pods show repeated read() spikes at model shard mmap offsets, with >2000 major page faults in first 10s after start.
KV cache: Prefix cache eviction coincides with fallback ramp; cache-population delayed by cold model load causing cascading misses.

Autoscaler logs: weight-decay-triggered scale-down at 11:17 UTC and cooldown of 30s; fallback threshold evaluated immediately after leading to routing change. Change came from autoscaler config PR 9f2c3e4 merged 2026-03-11.
Pod diagnostics: /var/log/syslog indicates swap usage grew to 1.4GB and kernel OOM scan invoked but no OOM kill. Paging increases request latency substantially on CPU replicas.

Routing policy: fallback decisions are threshold-based with a short evaluation window (config: fallback_evaluation_ms=500). Under bursty QPS, this window may mis-evaluate temporary dips in dedicated capacity.
Repro playbook: Synthetic load reproduces P99 ~9s when edge-cpu fallback is used; warm-edge replicas have P99 <500ms.
Related changelogs: runtime allocator reverted in artifact build 2026-03-08; quantized pipeline uses older glibc page-alignment behavior.
temporary_workarounds: Pin NovaDocs routing to dedicated-gpu-1 (applied 2026-03-12 14:30 UTC) — reduced customer impact immediately.
Increased fallback_evaluation_ms to 1500 for impacted pool to reduce premature fallback decisions (rolled as experiment to canary subset).
Advised NovaDocs to stagger bursts and enable request queuing at their edge for short-term mitigation.
next_steps: Patch runtime allocator/quantized artifact to reduce initial RSS and mmap churn (PR in progress: runtime#1189).
Roll back autoscaler weight-decay change or tune cooldown and evaluation window to avoid triggering fallback during transient load spikes.
Add a safeguard: prefer warm replicas with recent successful KV-cache hits for a brief sticky window after scale events.
Follow-up runbook update: document fallback thresholds and include a checklist for emergency routing pinning for high-tier customers.
resolution_notes: Workaround (routing pin) applied and customer confirmed immediate improvement. Patch for quantized allocator under review; autoscaler change reverted in canary. Will coordinate postmortem and permanent fix rollout. ETA for full fix: 2026-03-20.
resolution_status: Mitigated - workaround in place, fix pending
